    Cosmic Civilisations · Statistics of Cosmic Civilisations

    How long is the technological phase?

    Four historical alternatives, each with a probability and a mean duration. Ada computes the weighted mean. These are subjective assumptions about a communication-oriented technological phase, not a forecast for humanity, and the end of that phase is not automatically an extinction.

    L = Σ pᵢ lᵢ, with each probability used as a fraction.

    Intellectronics · Return to Earth

    What does persistent doubling imply?

    A normalised index starts at 1. The doubling time of 15 years follows a historical discussion of scientific periodicals. The year 2026 only places that horizon on a calendar. Ada computes one exponential. It is a scenario, not a forecast.

    N = N₀ · 2^(t / d)

    The factor is 2^(t / d) even when the starting quantity is zero. The quantity is then zero.

    The same exponential applies for the whole horizon. A shorter doubling time is not a tipping point.

    A whole year from -10000 to 10000. 2026 is a presentation choice, not a measured date.

    Illustrative level. The default 10 is not a forecast.

    Phantomology · Teletaxy and Phantomultiplication

    How long before a reply can return?

    Teletaxy is action at a distance. A signal here travels at the speed of light in vacuum, over a distance that does not change. The same wait is why an interstellar conversation cannot stay prompt. The presets are familiar examples, not one formula taken from the book.

    Variable distances use a chosen alignment, not today’s positions. Europa and Titan lie beyond their planets, not at the planet’s distance from the Sun. Proxima Centauri is the nearest star of Alpha Centauri, not the A and B pair.

    Signal arrives

    Reply arrives

    Timeline

      Sources and exact seconds

      Vacuum speed of light: 299,792,458 m/s, the SI definition of the metre. Astronomical unit: 149,597,870,700 m exactly, IAU 2012 Resolution B2; the Earth–Sun preset is 1 au. Light-year: one Julian year of 365.25 days of 86,400 s, as recognised by the IAU. Moon: NASA’s stated average, 384,400 km. Venus: NASA fact sheet, mean distance at inferior conjunction, 41.39 million km. Mars: 225 million km, a round figure for the often cited average of about 140 million miles. Europa: NASA’s mean Jupiter opposition, 628.81 million km, plus Europa’s orbital distance 671,000 km on the far side. Titan: difference of the NASA Saturn and Earth semimajor axes, 1,282.443 million km, plus Titan’s orbital distance 1,222,000 km on the far side. Proxima Centauri, Alpha Centauri C: 4.2465 light-years from the Gaia DR3 parallax. None of these is today’s ephemeris.

      A Lampoon of Evolution · Constructing Life

      How much information fits in a given time?

      Constructing Life sets three unlike historical figures side by side: a low-redundancy printed page of about 10,000 bits, a human mind coping with about 25 bits each second, and a bacterium producing at least 1,000 bits each second. This card divides a quantity by a constant rate, or multiplies that rate by a duration. It does not show that a bacterium reads a page, and 25 bits/s is not a measured brain bandwidth.

      Lem’s example restores 10,000 bits, 25 bits/s and 400 s, and draws the human and bacterial curves.

        Digital link, nominal line rate

        This is the nominal 1000 Mb/s line rate of IEEE 802.3 1000BASE-T. It is not framed payload, not a measured processing speed, and not machine understanding. The time is an ideal constant rate for the quantity above. When this rate is chosen, the chart compares it with the human figure only.

        Nominal line rate

        Time for this quantity at that rate

        The historical human and bacterial figures are not the same kind of information as each other, or as this line rate. Spike counts, DNA alphabet capacity and task information are not on the chart.

        Sources and what is not compared

        The three figures are the historical comparison in Stanisław Lem, Summa Technologiae, Constructing Life.

        The digital reference is the nominal 1000 Mb/s operation in IEEE Std 802.3 (1000BASE-T, originally IEEE 802.3ab-1999; the GMII in Clause 35 supports only 1000 Mb/s). One megabit is 1,000,000 bits. The time divides the quantity by 1,000,000,000 bits/s and ignores framing, interpacket gaps and encoding, so it is not payload throughput.

        Technical demonstration

        Add two numbers

        These two numbers are already filled in. Change either one and the sum updates. Ada does the addition. This is a boundary test, not a chapter calculator.

        Result

        Use a dot as the decimal separator in every language. Ada receives the binary64 value, not translated text.

        Contract: finite binary64 addition. A negative finite operand is an ordinary value. A non-finite operand or a non-finite sum is an error. Underflow to a finite result, including zero, is success. Tolerance for the published integer fixtures is exact binary64 equality.
